niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” connected-TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, industry, geography and whether you need media buying, programmatic tech, creative production, or measurement/attribution. Below I’ll give a short framework to help you pick, plus examples of strong players by category and the key questions to ask.

Short answer
- If you want full-service global reach and integrated TV/digital planning: look to major media holding companies (GroupM, Omnicom, Publicis, Dentsu, IPG, Havas).
- If you want programmatic CTV expertise and direct platform access: consider specialist agencies and DSPs (Simulmedia, Cadent, The Trade Desk) and platform partners (Roku Advertising, FreeWheel/Comcast, Magnite).
- If creative for large-screen storytelling is your priority: pick a creative agency or a production partner with proven CTV spots and advanced ad formats.

Examples of strong options by need
- Full-service / media buying (planning + buying + analytics): GroupM (Mindshare/Wavemaker), OMD/PHD (Omnicom), Zenith/Spark Foundry (Publicis), Carat (Dentsu), Initiative/UM (IPG).
- Programmatic/targeting specialists: The Trade Desk (DSP), Simulmedia (CTV-focused planning), Cadent (addressable TV/platform), Magnite (SSP), SpotX/Index Exchange (supply partners).
- Platform/Publisher direct solutions: Roku Advertising, Hulu, Peacock/Comcast FreeWheel, Amazon OTT, Samsung Ads.
- Creative & production for CTV: large creative networks (R/GA, Anomaly, Wieden+Kennedy) or boutique CTV-focused production shops (ask for case studies).

How to choose (criteria)
- Audience targeting: do they have/activate first‑party and identity solutions that match your target segments?
- Inventory access: premium publishers (Hulu, Roku, Tubi, Peacock) vs. long tail programmatic inventory.
- Measurement & outcomes: viewability, completion rate, incremental reach, attribution to site actions or offline lift (brand lift, MTA).
- Transparency & fees: media transparency, reporting cadence, what fees/markup they charge.
- Creative capability: ability to produce and optimize 16:9/landscape CTV creatives, interactive units, dynamic creative.
- Fraud & brand safety: verification partners (IAS, DoubleVerify), pre-bid blocking.
- Case studies & references: similar category, KPIs, budgets, and measurable results.
- Tech integrations: DSP/SSP partners, data management platform (DMP), clean-room access for data matching.

Questions to ask any agency/partner
- Can you show CTV case studies with KPIs similar to ours (brand lift, CVRs, CPA)?
- Which publishers/platforms do you buy from directly vs programmatically?
- What targeting options do you use (household, device, behavioral, contextual)?
- How do you measure viewability, completion, and conversions? Can you provide raw reporting?
- What are your fees/how is media priced (markup, percentage, flat fee)?
- What fraud and brand-safety vendors do you use?
- Can you run a pilot or proof-of-value test? What will you optimize on?

Recommended next step
If you tell me your goals (brand awareness, direct response), monthly or campaign budget, geography, and industry, I can:
- Recommend 3–5 agencies/platforms that fit your needs, or
- Draft an RFP checklist you can send to prospects.

Which of those would you prefer?
